--- title: "Instalment agreements, defaults on them and protest of VAT (ICMS) CDAs" description: "How common are instalment requests and protest on VAT (ICMS) certificates, and how does later recovery differ?" date: 2026-11-04 jupyter: python3 --- **Status:** exploration. Aggregates only. ::: {.callout-warning title="The status columns are not dated"} The instalment status and the protest status are the status at extraction. They are not the status on the enrolment date. An association between a request and later recovery is not a causal effect. ::: ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Source: VAT (ICMS) legal-entity extract, DuckDB read only. Window: 2016–2025. Rows after 2025 stay out of every table and every figure. Suppression: a cell with 1 to 4 distinct CNPJs is pooled as 'others (suppressed)'. A pool that still has fewer than 5 CNPJs is left blank. The count of pooled cells is printed with each table. Q1. Active = RFB code 02 (ATIVA). Inactive = codes 01, 03, 04, 08 (nula, suspensa, inapta, baixada). No establishment match, a root-only match, or any other code = unknown. Unknown is not forced into collectable or uncollectable. Q2. Payment history uses unit cnpj_root, scope vat_icms, denominator enrolled_value. The share is payments over enrolled value in the 5 calendar years that end in the reference year. The threshold is 10%. The unit's CDAs in the December snapshot enter the sum. The history is VAT (ICMS) only. Q3. Reference dates requested: 31 December of 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. A year with no December snapshot is printed and left out of the tables. December 2024 is a partial snapshot because of a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05). Later recovery is the next calendar year, and the sum from the next year through 2025, each divided by the December stock. Q4. Precedence: suspended → guaranteed → instalment → unknown → active_history → inactive_history → active_recent → inactive_no_history → active_old. Suspended is uncollectable first. The guaranteed line is always emitted and is empty. no guarantee table in the data; collectable share is understated. Q5. Age bands (0, 2], (2, 5], (5, 10], >10. A value equal to a break stays in the lower band (left-closed is false). Ages from 0 to the first break are the first band. Both readings are shown: the annual paid/stock rate, and the cumulative recovery of cohorts enrolled in the window. The band above the last break is not observable on those cohorts. Q6. The outcome is any payment in the year, the same outcome as model 1 of the payment section. When the eligible frame is larger than 100,000 certificate-years, the fit uses a stratified sample of that size (year, origin, and the payment outcome), seed 2026. Standard errors are HC1. Clustered standard errors by CNPJ root are the column beside them. This is an association. It is not a forecast. Q7. One lab entry per block. Q8. The proposal material reports mean collection 1.38% against a collectable share 27.05%. The material states neither the year nor the tax cut. This page does not reproduce those two figures. It reports the analogous VAT (ICMS) legal-entity account. Registry attributes are the RFB extract 2026-03, which is later than the debts. CNAE enters as the division (two digits). ``` ::: ::: ## Question What share of VAT (ICMS) certificates has an instalment request, how often a request is broken, and how does recovery differ for certificates with and without a request, a break or a protest? ## Data The setup cell prints the window and the source. The instalment table and the protest table link to the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract by the debt id. Both tables cover enrolments from the start of the window. Certificates enrolled before the window stay out of these shares. ## Method A request date or a break date outside the window is counted and left unchanged. It is not used as an event time, and an impossible break date does not close a request. The share with a request is the number of certificates with a valid request date divided by the certificates enrolled inside the window. Recovery is the sum of GARE amounts divided by the sum of enrolled values. The time from enrolment to the first request, from the request to a valid break, and from enrolment to a valid protest date uses the Kaplan–Meier estimator $$\hat S(t)=\prod_{t_j\le t}\left(1-\frac{d_j}{n_j}\right)$$ The curve shows $1-\hat S(t)$. $d_j$ is the number of events in month $t_j$ and $n_j$ is the number of certificates still at risk. Certificates with no event by the end of the window are censored. A point with fewer certificates at risk than the suppression floor is hidden. Kaplan and Meier (1958) define the estimator. *Reference:* Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 53(282), 457–481. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452 ## How to read In the share chart, the horizontal axis is the enrolment year and the vertical axis is the share of certificates with a request. Compare origins. A higher line is a higher share. It is not a recovery rate. In a Kaplan–Meier chart, the horizontal axis is months since the start of the spell and the vertical axis is the share that has had the event. A steeper line is an earlier event. The curve is not a causal effect of the instalment or of the protest. ::: {#tbl-date-quality .cell tbl-cap='Impossible dates. Counted and left unchanged.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Dates outside the window, and break years before year 1000, are flagged. They are not rewritten. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## What not to conclude The tables cover enrolments inside the window. They do not describe older certificates. The status is the extraction status. A higher recovery for certificates with a request is an association. It is not the effect of granting the instalment, and it is not the effect of the protest. A payment is not the same thing as recovery of the whole credit. The comparison of amounts before and after the protest date is descriptive. The protest date is not assigned by an experiment.
